{{Top|leg|title=''Mir'shupur'' sigil}}
{{Conjecture|legends}}
{{Quote|He was worried about me.''"<br />"''He saw the sigil on your ''buy'ce''. It told him you were disabled and why. Saves a lot of daft questions, you see, and folks know how to treat you.|Fi Skirata and Parja Bralor|<ref name="O66">''[[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel]]''</ref>}}
In [[Mandalorian/Legends|Mandalorian]] culture, individuals who had suffered debilitating [[Brain/Legends|brain]] trauma could mark their [[Armor/Legends|armor]] with a unique '''sigil''' that would indicate their condition to any who saw it. The sigil was comprised of the [[Mandalorian (writing system)/Legends|Mandalorian runes]] for ''M'' and ''S'', and short for the word ''mir'shupur''—"brain injury," when translated from [[Mando'a/Legends|''Mando'a'']] to [[Galactic Basic Standard/Legends|Basic]]. It served to notify others of the wearer's disability, while at the same time acting as a badge of honor recognizing the wounded individual's prior service. Mandalorians who saw the ''mir'shupur'' sigil on another's armor knew to treat the wearer gently, and to offer ready aid should they appear to be in need of it.<ref name="O66" />

In the [[Standard year/Legends|year]] [[19 BBY/Legends|19 BBY]], after being taken to [[Mandalore/Legends|Mandalore]] following a traumatic brain injury [[Battle of Gaftikar|suffered]] on [[Gaftikar]] that left him temporarily brain [[Death/Legends|dead]], the former [[Clone commando/Legends|Republic commando]] [[Fi Skirata]] had his helmet adorned with the ''mir'shupur'' sigil by his girlfriend [[Parja Bralor]]. While waiting for Bralor one [[Standard day/Legends|day]] in [[Enceri]]'s marketplace, Skirata's sigil attracted the attention<ref name="O66" /> of former [[Mandalore (title)/Legends|''Mand'alor'']] [[Spar]],<ref name="HotM">{{InsiderCite|80|The History of the Mandalorians: Exploring the Evolution of a Mighty Race of Warriors}}</ref> who stayed with the wounded soldier and kept him company until Bralor arrived. Shortly after, while ordering at an [[Enceri cantina]], Skirata's ''mir'shupur'' sigil softened the demeanor of the [[Unidentified female bartender|elderly bartender]] waiting on him; while initially been suspicious of his inability to speak ''Mando'a'' as most other Enceri residents did, she quickly warmed to the injured veteran upon realizing his condition.<ref name="O66" />

==Behind the scenes==
The ''mir'shupur'' sigil was first introduced to the ''[[Star Wars]]'' universe in the ''[[Republic Commando]]'' novel [[Order 66: A Republic Commando Novel|''Order 66'']], written by [[Author/Legends|author]] [[Karen Traviss]] and published [[September 16]], [[2008]].
